title: Token reference
description: Every base token, palette entry, and theme key, and what each falls back to.
icon: Table
---

A theme has three levels: **base tokens** (required), a **palette** (optional), and **theme keys** (optional). This page lists all of them.

Every theme key resolves in the same order:

1. The value you set in `keys`.
2. The palette entry the key derives from, if the key has one and you set it.
3. The base token the key derives from, if the key has one.
4. An Atlas default for the active appearance.

A key that derives its colour is often transformed on the way: given a transparency, lightened, or mixed toward the background. Those transforms apply only while deriving. A value you write in `keys` is used exactly as written.

## Base tokens

All 45 are required in every variant. Leave one out and the file will not load. The names are shadcn/ui's, unchanged.

### Surfaces and text

| Token | Colours |
|---|---|
| `background`, `foreground` | the app background and default text |
| `card`, `card-foreground` | elevated panels |
| `popover`, `popover-foreground` | menus, popovers, and overlay panels |
| `primary`, `primary-foreground` | the signature colour: active tab indicator, selection tint, marching-ants stroke |
| `secondary`, `secondary-foreground` | secondary surfaces and their text |
| `muted`, `muted-foreground` | muted surfaces, dimmed text, comments, line numbers |
| `accent`, `accent-foreground` | the shadcn hover surface: active tab background, bracket match |
| `destructive`, `destructive-foreground` | destructive actions, and the fallback for error colours |
| `border` | separators and control borders |
| `input` | input borders |
| `ring` | the keyboard focus ring, and strong borders |
| `chart-1` … `chart-5` | chart series |
| `sidebar`, `sidebar-foreground` | panel and rail backgrounds, and their text |
| `sidebar-primary`, `sidebar-primary-foreground` | the signature colour inside a panel |
| `sidebar-accent`, `sidebar-accent-foreground` | a panel's hover surface |
| `sidebar-border` | low-emphasis separators |
| `sidebar-ring` | focus inside a panel |

### Radius, type, and elevation

| Token | Notes |
|---|---|
| `radius` | the whole radius scale derives from it: controls at `radius − 4`, cards at `radius − 2`, popovers at `radius`, dialogs at `radius + 4`. Use a pixel value. The built-in themes all use `8px`. |
| `font-sans` | the interface font stack |
| `font-mono` | the editor, terminal, and code font stack |
| `font-serif` | required by the shadcn set; Atlas has no serif surface |
| `tracking-normal` | required by the shadcn set; Atlas does not currently read it |
| `spacing` | Atlas's density is built on the default `0.25rem`, which every built-in theme uses |
| `shadow-sm` | the raised elevation |
| `shadow-xl`, `shadow-2xl` | `shadow-2xl` is the menu and popover elevation; a dialog stacks `shadow-xl` beneath it |
| `shadow-2xs`, `shadow-xs`, `shadow-md`, `shadow-lg` | required by the shadcn set; Atlas renders three elevations and does not use these four |

<Callout type="info">
  Give a light variant its own shadow values. Dark shadows copied across read as heavy halos on a pale background.
</Callout>

## Palette

Eight optional hues. Each one is the first source for a group of theme keys, so setting the palette is the cheapest way to make syntax, terminal, diff, and status colours belong to your theme.

| Hue | Feeds |
|---|---|
| `red` | error status, ANSI red, diff removals, `syntax.tag`, `syntax.regexp`, `syntax.builtin`, removed-line counts |
| `orange` | orange status, `syntax.number`, `syntax.constant`, `syntax.boolean`, `syntax.null`, the Claude chip |
| `yellow` | `text.accent`, warning status, ANSI yellow, `syntax.attribute`, `syntax.meta`, the Cursor and Kilo chips |
| `green` | success status, ANSI green, diff additions, `syntax.string`, unread indicators, added-line counts, capture, the GPT and Codex chips |
| `cyan` | ANSI cyan, `syntax.type`, `syntax.operator`, `syntax.property` |
| `blue` | informational status, ANSI blue, `diff.modified.background`, `syntax.function`, the Gemini chip |
| `purple` | purple status, ANSI magenta, `syntax.keyword`, the local-agent chip |
| `pink` | `syntax.escape`, the Amp chip |

Set as many or as few as you like. Each entry is looked up on its own.

## Theme keys

135 optional roles. The **Falls back to** column is what Atlas uses when you do not set the key; where that column is empty for a source, the next source in the chain applies, ending at an Atlas default for the active appearance.

### Borders

| Key | Colours | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `border.default` | default separator and control border | base `border` |
| `border.subtle` | low-emphasis separator | base `sidebar-border` |
| `border.variant` | alternate low-emphasis border | base `sidebar-border` |
| `border.strong` | high-emphasis border | base `ring` |
| `border.focus` | focused-control border | base `ring` |

### Interactive states

| Key | Colours | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `element.hover` | hover overlay on an ordinary element | base `foreground` at 4% |
| `element.selected` | selected overlay | base `foreground` at 6% |
| `element.active` | pressed overlay | base `foreground` at 8% |
| `element.highlight` | the top edge on a raised surface | base `foreground` at 6% |
| `element.primary_hover` | hovered signature-colour fill | base `primary`, lightened |
| `element.primary_muted` | muted signature-colour fill | base `primary` at 6% |
| `ghost_element.hover` | hover overlay on a ghost control | base `foreground` at 3% |
| `ghost_element.selected` | selected overlay on a ghost control | base `foreground` at 5% |
| `ghost_element.active` | pressed overlay on a ghost control | base `foreground` at 7% |
| `selection.background` | document text selection | base `primary` at 18% |

### Agent chips

Each agent has a foreground and a background, and the background is the same hue at 10%.

| Keys | Falls back to |
|---|---|
| `agent.claude.foreground`, `agent.claude.background` | palette `orange` |
| `agent.gpt.foreground`, `agent.gpt.background` | palette `green` |
| `agent.codex.foreground`, `agent.codex.background` | palette `green` |
| `agent.gemini.foreground`, `agent.gemini.background` | palette `blue` |
| `agent.local.foreground`, `agent.local.background` | palette `purple` |
| `agent.cursor.foreground`, `agent.cursor.background` | palette `yellow` |
| `agent.kilo.foreground`, `agent.kilo.background` | palette `yellow` |
| `agent.amp.foreground`, `agent.amp.background` | palette `pink` |
| `agent.opencode.foreground`, `agent.opencode.background` | base `muted-foreground` |

### Everything else

| Key | Colours | Falls back to |
|---|---|---|
| `capture.live` | the active capture indicator | palette `green` |
| `atlas.ants` | the animated marching-ants stroke | base `primary` |

## Where these end up

Atlas resolves the whole set on every theme change and writes it out as CSS custom properties. A base token becomes `--` plus its name, so `sidebar-border` is `--sidebar-border`. A theme key becomes `--atlas-` plus its name with dots and underscores turned into dashes, so `terminal.ansi.bright_red` is `--atlas-terminal-ansi-bright-red`.
